The '''1979–80 Bundesliga''' was the 17th season of the [[Bundesliga]], [[West Germany]]'s premier football league. It began on 11 August 1979<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dfb.de/index.php?id=328178 |title=Schedule Round 1 |publisher=DFB |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110608082440/https://www.dfb.de/index.php?id=328178 |archive-date=8 June 2011 }}</ref> and ended on 31 May 1980.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dfb.de/index.php?id=328540 |title=Archive 1979/1980 Round 34 |publisher=DFB |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110608082530/https://www.dfb.de/index.php?id=328540 |archive-date=8 June 2011 }}</ref> [[Hamburger SV]] were the defending champions.

==Competition modus==
Every team played two games against each other team, one at home and one away. Teams received two points for a win and one point for a draw. If two or more teams were tied on points, places were determined by [[goal difference]] and, if still tied, by goals scored. The team with the most points were crowned champions while the three teams with the fewest points were relegated to their respective [[2. Bundesliga]] divisions.

==Team changes to 1978–79==
[[Arminia Bielefeld]], [[1. FC Nürnberg]] and [[SV Darmstadt 98]] were relegated to the [[1979–80 2. Bundesliga|2. Bundesliga]] after finishing in the last three places. They were replaced by [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]], winners of the 2. Bundesliga Northern Division, [[TSV 1860 Munich]], winners of the Southern Division and [[KFC Uerdingen 05|Bayer Uerdingen]], who won a two-legged promotion play-off against [[SpVgg Bayreuth]].
